content_html_sanitized:
The real purpose for medical science is to avoid embarrassing doctors. For example, Spain Has the Highest Rate of Cannabis Use in Europe and Needs to Legalize It Even More Than Other Countries

 

But Spain has announced that it will only allow doctors to prescribe some sort of cannabis based treatments AS LONG AS IT IS PRESCRIBED BY A SPECIALIST AND ADMINISTERED IN A HOSPITAL!

 

Spain actually has an excellent healthcare system, but maybe they should study Dutch coffee shops? I have never seen a dead body in one.

 

El Pais, one of Spain’s leading newspapers, reported, The Government approves the use of medicinal cannabis: only in hospitals and prescribed by specialist. “The royal decree drafted by the Ministry of Health does not specify the ailments that can be treated, which will be adjusted to scientific evidence.” WOW! Really?

 

The real “scientific” purpose here is avoiding embarrassment for the medical/scientific community which has pretended that cannabis has no medical value, but is being forced to, sort of, kind of, well maybe…

 

As El Pais observed in an editorial, “Despite attempts by some left-wing groups in recent years, the legalization of recreational cannabis use is not in sight in the short term. The government's decision could reignite the necessary discussion that other developed countries have already addressed regarding the consumption, cultivation, and sale of a substance that is normalized in society (almost 44% of Spaniards aged 15 to 64 admit to having used it). At some point, we will have to confront a multi-million-dollar business that fosters mafia-like practices. For now, this is a realistic step with concrete benefits.” Yep.

 

Be grateful for small favors.

 

Meanwhile, in France,  CannabisHealth.co.uk is optimistic, reporting, France Plans to “Fully Integrate” Medical Cannabis into its Healthcare System

But only after France Making An Even Bigger Mess of Its Cannabis Policy, But Finally About to Legalize Medical After Only Thirty Years

 

Meanwhile in Germany, where 60% of the people favor legalizing cannabis, “The German federal government has presented a cabinet resolution on changes to the prescription and dispensing of medical cannabis. According to the draft, initial prescriptions will only be possible after personal consultation with a doctor. Follow-up prescriptions would be permitted every four quarters under the same conditions, and in between via telemedicine. Furthermore, cannabis flowers should only be dispensed in local pharmacies.”

See

Cannabis and Democracy: Who Are Our Leaders Following? It Ain't Us!

 

Spain and France and all the other countries that are delaying not only recreational cannabis, but also medical cannabis, are not just ignoring their citizens, but ignoring basic science.

 

Medical science does not change when it crosses borders. Cannabis works exactly the same in Spain, or France or Germany….

Or even in The Netherlands!!!

See

From The MarijuanaNews Archives 2003: “Now It's Official: Dutch Pharmacies Provide Medical Cannabis Covered by Health Insurance.” Updated for Telemedicine and Current Data

 

Meanwhile, in the Czech Republic, all doctors in Czechia can prescribe medicinal cannabis.In a further step to liberalize marijuana legislation, patients will also receive a three-month supply of the medicine, rather than just one.

 

The sad fact is that the medical profession and the various government regulatory agencies have totally disqualified themselves by treating their patients without regard for basic scientific principles.

 

They are simply making matters worse by pretending that these delays are serving some kind of medical or scientific purpose.
